To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CCndnS improves the performance of in-network caches in NDN and that its performance can be predicted accurately with a simple analytical model.

CCndnS reduces redundant copies of popular content and unpopular content, reduces memory latency, increases hit rates in core without reducing edge hit rates, balances load among caches, and decouples caches, thus allowing for a simple analytical performance modeling of the network of caches.
CCndnS, a caching strategy for NDN, addresses the four issues of in-network caching, and that a simple analytical model of the network of caches is accurate.

the design and analysis of a content-centric network architecture that can scale to large networks.
a novel approach to the problem of caching in information centric networking (ICN).
the design and performance analysis of a novel caching strategy for Named data Networking (NDN) that addresses the above issues and provides a tractable model for the network performance.

CCndnS reduces cache pollution and improves hit rates in the network core without reducing hit rate at the edge and load balancing.
